text: The device hums. Water everywhere, as far as you can see. High on a mountain, the ark sits still.
But God remembered Noah and all the animals and livestock that were with him in the ark. And God sent a wind over the earth, and the waters began to subside.
On the seventeenth day of the seventh month, the ark came to rest on the mountains of Ararat.

speaker: Noah
text: {name}! Watch. We will see if the land is dry yet.

speaker: Noah
text: God has kept us safe all this time.
After months inside the ark, everyone squints in the sunlight.
The ark's window is open.
After forty days Noah opened the window he had made in the ark and sent out a raven. It kept flying back and forth until the waters had dried up from the earth.
But the dove found no place to rest her foot, and she returned to him in the ark, because the waters were still covering the surface of all the earth. …
Noah waited seven more days and again sent out the dove from the ark.
The dove lands on your hand. In her beak is a fresh green leaf.
And behold, the dove returned to him in the evening with a freshly plucked olive leaf in her beak. So Noah knew that the waters had receded from the earth.
And Noah waited seven more days and sent out the dove again, but this time she did not return to him.
… So Noah removed the covering from the ark and saw that the surface of the ground was dry.

speaker: God
text: Come out of the ark, you and your wife, along with your sons and their wives. Bring out all the living creatures that are with you—birds, livestock, and everything that crawls upon the ground—so that they can spread out over the earth and be fruitful and multiply upon it.
The two of them follow you.
Take this pair down first.
They run off across the new grass.
They are free to roam now.
Open land, green again after the flood.
Every living creature, every creeping thing, and every bird—everything that moves upon the earth—came out of the ark, kind by kind.

speaker: Noah
text: {name}, help me gather stones. We will build an altar and thank the LORD.
You are already carrying a stone.
A rock, washed clean by the flood.
A good, heavy stone. Bring it to Noah.
Noah is waiting for stones.
Noah fits the stone into place.
Then Noah built an altar to the LORD. And taking from every kind of clean animal and clean bird, he offered burnt offerings on the altar.

speaker: God
text: As long as the earth endures, seedtime and harvest, cold and heat, summer and winter, day and night shall never cease.

speaker: God
text: And I establish My covenant with you: Never again will all life be cut off by the waters of a flood; never again will there be a flood to destroy the earth.

speaker: God
text: I have set My rainbow in the clouds, and it will be a sign of the covenant between Me and the earth.
God made a promise and put a sign of it in the sky. Every rainbow is a reminder that God keeps His promises.

speaker: Noah
text: A whole new world, {name}. And God's promise over all of it.

The LORD sits enthroned over the flood; the LORD is enthroned as King forever.

text: My father says we are to fill the earth again.
